history.summary: A Maheshwar Temple at Rampur Bushahr is listed among the town's ancient temples as a shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva on the banks of the Sutlej River, set in lush greenery and regarded as a calm, historic place of worship (gettoplists.com, which groups it with Rampur's Raghunath and Narsingh temples). No founder, dynasty, built date or exact siting is recorded in accessible sources, so the entry is thin. IDENTITY UNCERTAINTY: there is also a well-documented Maheshwar Temple at Sungra, Kinnaur district - about 62 km from Rampur, a three-storeyed pagoda-style wooden shrine dedicated to Mahadev Shiva that has been dated to the 8th century AD (hindu-calendar.com). That Sungra temple is a different, separately documented temple and is NOT this file's referent; this file covers only the thinly documented Rampur-town Sutlej-bank shrine named by gettoplists. Coordinates are approximate Rampur-town coordinates (wikimapia: 31 deg 26'59"N 77 deg 37'47"E), since no POI-level position for the shrine was found.

name: Maheshwar Temple
town_description: Rampur Bushahr is a historic town on the Sutlej River in Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh - the last capital of the Bushahr princely state and a former trading centre on the old Hindustan-Tibet Road, known for Padam Palace and the annual Lavi Fair.

travel.airport: Shimla Airport (Jubbarhatti), about 130 km from Rampur.
travel.railway: Nearest railhead: Shimla (narrow-gauge), about 130 km away; Kalka (broad gauge) is farther.
travel.road: On NH-5 (the old Hindustan-Tibet Road), about 130 km from Shimla; regular buses and taxis connect Rampur to Shimla and nearby towns.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and October to November; Maha Shivaratri (February-March) is the main festival for Shiva shrines.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published online; daytime darshan typical of small-town temples.
